newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa stirred up by weak stg but gains capped.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa stirred up by weak stg but gains capped.

text.p: A weaker sterling helped London cocoa futures tick higher on Monday but there was little else to pull the market out of its protracted downtrend, traders said.
Cocoa drew some support from an increase in U.S. speculative short positions detailed in the latest CFTC Commitment of Traders Report on Friday, although the longs still outnumbered the shorts.
But many soft commodity traders were caught up in coffee's surge in the afternoon partly linked to news Vietnam could join a producer group that has an export retention programme in place.

LIFFE's key March cocoa position gained three stg on the day to 881 stg a tonne, ending just below the session high of 883. It lacked the motivation to step closer to 900 which is seen necessary to boost the technical prospects.
Instead, "people occasionally come in and pick the bottom," was how one trader described Monday's modest gains.
Deals were confined to mixed trade activity. But further forward contracts like the distant July and Sept managed to chalk up bigger gains, up 11 and 10 stg respectively.

The day's turnover of 5,362 lots also included some 1,500 lots of AAs, mostly in March, while switches were mostly steady with March/may at 20-21 stg, March/July at 41, March/Sept at 61 and March/Dec at 70.
Currency factors stirred in some arbitrage deals as players bought London against the dollar-denominated New York.

The latest CFTC report showed a rise in speculative shorts (including non-commercial and non-reportable positions) of 5,443 lots to 22,543 in the two weeks to January 14 but speculators were still net long of 3,575 lots, suggesting the market was vulnerable to further long liquidation.
In other news, financial analysts expected Nestle SA to announce a seven percent rise in group sales on Tuesday due to weakening Swiss franc and volume growth.
Support comes in at 865 stg for March but remains shaky while the downtrend continues, technical analysts said.
